clue.text: Catcalls kill politician's quick pause

parts.note: jeering whistles from a crowd are catcalls
to top someone is slang for to kill them

explanation.surface: Jeering hecklers bring a politician's brief appearance to an abrupt end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kill' looks like a verb acting on the politician, but it just supplies the slang word for kill.
explanation.definitionFit: A whistle-stop is a brief halt on a campaign tour, originally at small railway stations, so a candidate's quick pause.

clue.text: I left callow men in WC being treated — but not here!

definitions.text: I left callow men in WC being treated — but not here!

indicators.note: being treated suggests processing or reworking, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left
the letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Someone walked out on immature men receiving medical care in a toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: men treated would not be at a clinic for women, hence 'but not here!'
explanation.definitionFit: A well woman clinic gives health checks to women only, so it is a place where men are not treated.

clue.text: Finally stripped, nothing excluded

indicators.note: stripped means bared of its outer covering, so the first and last letters are removed

parts.note: the word itself, taken as written

explanation.surface: At last fully undressed, with nothing held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' looks like a time adverb but is the word to be stripped of its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In all means in total, counting everything, so with nothing left out.

clue.text: Extra hot bath included in rent

indicators.note: included in puts one word inside another

parts.note: rent is the past tense of rend, so tore
a spa is a hot spring for bathing

explanation.surface: An additional hot bath comes as part of the rent payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like a payment for housing but is the past tense of rend, to tear.
explanation.definitionFit: Something to spare is surplus to requirements, so extra.

clue.text: RAF plea produced protective part of cap

indicators.note: produced means made or fashioned, so these letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: An appeal from the air force led to a new bit of headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAF is the Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: An earflap is the flap on a cap that folds down to protect the ear from cold.

clue.text: Bring round carpeting that's no good

indicators.note: no good tells the solver to take away the letter that stands for good

parts.note: a carpeting is a scolding, a talking-to
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Persuading someone by giving them a pointless dressing-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpeting' looks like floor covering but is British slang for a reprimand, being 'on the carpet' before the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring someone round is to persuade them, and to talk someone into something is to persuade them too.

clue.text: Just missing the last mail collection?

definitions.text: Just missing the last mail collection?

parts.words: Just missing the last mail collection?
parts.note: surface reading: arriving at the postbox moments after the final collection; setter's reading: an idiom for being beaten narrowly at the finish line, the post being the winning post

explanation.walkthrough: The post of the idiom is the winning post at the end of a race, not the mail.
explanation.definitionFit: To be beaten at the very finish is to just miss out, which the idiom describes using the racing post.

clue.text: Complete course, we're told, with fork

indicators.note: we're told means as spoken to us, so the word is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: a course is a route, which can be said like 'root'
and means with
a fork in a road or tree is a branch

explanation.surface: Directions for a full journey including a fork in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: Route rhymes with 'shoot' in British speech, so it sounds like root.
explanation.definitionFit: Root and branch describes change that is thorough and total, so complete.

clue.text: Working allotment here? I don't believe it!

indicators.note: working means being worked on, so the letters are reshaped into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed to hear a gardener is actually tending their plot.
explanation.walkthrough: An allotment is a small rented plot for growing vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Tell me another is a scornful retort to a tall story, the same disbelief as the exclamation.

clue.text: Liquid containers, outsize 1 litre example included

indicators.note: something included is put inside something else, so the middle pieces sit within the size label

parts.note: OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize
the Roman numeral for one
L is the abbreviation for litre
a can is one example of a container for liquid, referring back to the definition

explanation.surface: A list of drinks containers, one of them an oversized one-litre example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Example' points back to the definition: the container it gives is one instance of the liquid containers being defined, making the clue partly self-referential.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil cans are vessels made to hold and pour lubricating oil, so they are containers for a liquid.

clue.text: 'e's paler, suffering setback?

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad way, damaged, so the letters before it are knocked out of order

parts.note: the letters of these words, with the dropped aitch of he's

explanation.surface: A cockney voice asks whether a man looking pale has taken a turn for the worse.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'e's is just a dropped H in the surface; only its letters count.
explanation.definitionFit: A relapse is a falling back into illness after improvement, which is a setback in recovery.

clue.text: Rough lower blocks behind bathroom fitting

indicators.note: something that blocks a passage sits inside it, so these letters lodge within the other word

parts.note: the tail is what is behind, at the back

indicators.note: rough suggests crude or disordered, so the word that follows is roughed up into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A clumsy lower part obstructs a fitting at the back of the bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough lower' reads as a description of some bathroom part, but 'lower' is just letters to be jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: A towel rail is a bar fixed to a bathroom wall for hanging towels, a typical bathroom fitting.

clue.text: Perfect trader's assertion

definitions.meaning: first meaning: flawless, the best one could hope for
second meaning, split in two: what a trader might declare

explanation.surface: A merchant claims his goods are flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is read as two words, I DEAL, the statement of someone who trades.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means matching one's highest standard, which is what perfect means.

clue.text: Two thirds of company unable to move

indicators.note: taking two thirds of a word leaves its opening part and drops the final third

parts.note: a number is a company or group, as in 'one of our number'

explanation.surface: Most of a firm has frozen and cannot shift.
explanation.walkthrough: Of a six-letter word, two thirds is the first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Numb describes a limb with no feeling and often no power of movement, so unable to move.

clue.text: Utter a peep when startled but carry on

indicators.note: a startled person jumps about, so the letters before are scattered into another order

parts.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Advice to let out a small squeak when surprised, then just continue.
explanation.definitionFit: To perpetuate something is to keep it going indefinitely, which is to carry it on.

clue.text: Disapproves of one's child supporting father

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting means sitting underneath, so these pieces come after the other

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
one's own means belonging to oneself
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A parent scorning their own boy who props up his dad.
explanation.definitionFit: To frown on something is to show disapproval of it.

clue.text: Carey Street ruin

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Carey Street is the London street where the ... court once stood, so 'in Carey Street' means insolvent

explanation.walkthrough: Carey Street is a London street that housed the bankruptcy court; British idiom uses its name for the state of being bankrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: Bankruptcy is the legal state of being unable to pay debts, which is financial ruin.

clue.text: Threaten servant carrying on with son

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the servant word wraps round the rest

parts.note: a page is a boy servant
re means on, concerning
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A household servant menaces his master while holding a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrying on' reads as one phrase meaning behaving badly; split, 'carrying' is the container and 'on' gives RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To presage is to foreshadow something bad, as a gathering storm threatens rain.

clue.text: Wasn't able to locate dissident leaders held by nobleman

indicators.note: held by means kept inside, so the selected letters go within the title

parts.note: a count is a nobleman

indicators.note: leaders are the ones at the front, so the opening letter of each word is taken

parts.note: the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Failing to find the rebel ringleaders sheltered by an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' belongs to the definition, since the answer is followed by a bare verb just as 'wasn't able to' is.
explanation.definitionFit: Couldn't is the contracted could not, which means was not able to do something.

clue.text: Grim king's taken out old machine gun

indicators.note: taken out means removed, so the royal letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: stern means grim, severe
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A grim monarch has been shot down with a vintage automatic weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken out' suggests an assassination, but it just means the R is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sten was a cheap British submachine gun of the Second World War, so an old machine gun.

clue.text: Sanction that hurt everyone at first

indicators.note: at first says which piece comes at the front when the two are joined

parts.note: all means everyone
the cry someone makes when something hurts

explanation.surface: Approving something that caused pain to all at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are read in reverse clue order because 'at first' puts everyone in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction is to give official permission, which is to allow something.

clue.text: Like an enthusiast briefly intimidated in hospital department

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the word is lost

parts.note: to be bullied is to be intimidated

explanation.surface: A keen patient found feeling cowed in a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: ENT, ear nose and throat, is the hospital department crosswords use most.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebullient means bubbling over with energy and cheer, as a keen enthusiast is.

clue.text: Reason serviceman stabs upstanding officer

indicators.note: stabs means goes into, so the serviceman sits inside the officer
in a down entry, upstanding means reading bottom to top, so the officer is turned around

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: The reason a soldier knifed his worthy commanding officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upstanding' looks like praise for the officer but is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Logic is sound reasoning, and reason as a noun means the same faculty.

clue.text: Game helping to make American a star

indicators.note: helping to make means forming part of, so the answer is a portion of the words that follow

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the next two

explanation.surface: A game that turns a US player into a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-style card game played with two packs, so a game.

clue.text: D****d setter's possibly snuffed it

parts.note: a setter is a breed of dog; 'possibly' marks it as an example, and the 's is 'is'
someone who has snuffed it has died, is gone

explanation.surface: The puzzle setter has died, with a censored curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the crossword compiler, but it is the gundog. The asterisks stand for 'damned', and doggone is a mild American substitute for that oath.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggone is a euphemistic American form of damned, matching the asterisked swear word.

clue.text: Associate and I share part of America

parts.note: to associate things is to connect them
taken as written
a cut is a share, as of profits

explanation.surface: Someone claims a share in a slice of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Connecticut is one of the New England states, so a part of the United States of America.
